calculator.title: IRR Calculator
calculator.description: Calculate the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) for insurance savings products.
calculator.irrDesc1: IRR is the discount rate that makes the Net Present Value (NPV) of all cash flows equal to zero.
calculator.irrDesc2: Premiums are negative cash flows; surrender/maturity values are positive cash flows.
calculator.irrDesc3: Higher IRR means better actual return on the insurance product.
calculator.irrDesc4: IRR is the fairest metric for comparing different products.
calculator.irrDesc5: Data should come from official product brochures, never guess.

IRRSEO.quickAnswerText: Insurance IRR (Internal Rate of Return) is the annualized rate of return on an insurance policy, accounting for premium payments and future cash values. Use our free calculator to compare savings plans.
IRRSEO.seoParagraph1: The Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is the most accurate way to compare insurance savings products. Unlike simple return calculations, IRR accounts for the timing of all cash flows — premium payments and future withdrawals — giving you a true annualized return.
IRRSEO.seoParagraph2: When comparing Hong Kong participating policies or mainland China increasing sum insured products, IRR lets you see which product actually delivers better value over time.
IRRSEO.faqQ1: What is a good IRR for an insurance policy?
IRRSEO.faqA1: For long-term savings policies, an IRR of 3-5% is typical for guaranteed returns. Participating policies may show illustrated IRR of 4-7%, but non-guaranteed portions depend on the insurer's performance.
IRRSEO.faqQ2: How do I compare two insurance products using IRR?
IRRSEO.faqA2: Enter the premium payment details and expected cash values for each product. The product with the higher IRR provides better value for the same level of risk.
IRRSEO.faqA3: The calculator uses the Newton-Raphson method with bisection fallback for mathematical accuracy. Results depend on the cash values you enter — always use official product illustrations.
